title: Hinglish discourse fillers stripped by the formatter shift token indices
why_real: Real Indian dictation is full of discourse particles like 'matlab', 'um', and 'na' that the formatter strips entirely, so the ASR and formatted sentences have very different token counts and any positional mapping would land on the wrong word.

inputs.asr: matlab um i will ask priya na

expected.reason: Sequence alignment skips the stripped fillers on both ends and still locates the target token correctly.
